message.content:
The most recent estimates put the United States’ Gini coefficient at roughly **0.41** (or 41 %) for the year 2022.  

| Source | Year | Gini (US) |
|--------|------|-----------|
| OECD (Income inequality database) | 2021 | 0.41 |
| World Bank (World Development Indicators) | 2022 | 0.41 |
| U.S. Census Bureau (Poverty and Income Statistics) | 2022 | 0.41 |

> **Interpretation**  
> A Gini coefficient of 0 represents perfect equality (everyone has the same income), while a coefficient of 1 indicates perfect inequality (one person has all the income). A value of 0.41 places the U.S. among the higher‑inequality countries in the OECD, though it has been relatively stable over the past decade.

If you need the figure for a specific year or a different definition (e.g., pre‑tax vs. post‑tax), let me know and I can look up the exact dataset.
